thesis: The world's second-largest gold producer, with ~70% of output from Canada and Australia, a net cash position of $3.3B and an A- credit rating. Q2 2026 delivered record free cash flow of $1,335M on a realized gold price of $4,483/oz, and the Hope Bay, Odyssey and Detour Lake underground projects underpin a pathway to more than 4.0 million ounces by the early 2030s. The stock sits ~28% below its 52-week high as gold corrects from its August 2026 peak and the Barnat pit wall failure trims 2027-2028 output, which is what creates the entry point — and also the main risk if gold keeps sliding.

drivers: Gold re-rates back above $5,000/oz on renewed central bank buying and a dovish Fed pivot; several large banks publish $5,000-$6,300 targets
Barnat remediation completes on plan and the 2027-2028 production impact lands at the low end of the up-to-150koz-per-year guidance
Hope Bay (400-435koz/yr, after-tax IRR above 20% at $4,000/oz gold) and Odyssey Shaft #1 de-risk the 2030 production step-up
Ikkari and the consolidated 2,492 km2 Central Lapland land package deliver a reserve announcement that triggers CVR milestones and re-rates the Finnish asset base
Net cash plus the $2B internal NCIB limit funds aggressive buybacks at depressed multiples

base_case.assumptions: Gold averages $4,200-$4,700/oz through 2027. 2026 production lands near the lower end of the 3.3-3.5 million ounce guidance range with AISC inside the $1,400-$1,550/oz band. Capex stays at the guided $2.6-$2.8B excluding capitalized exploration. Roughly 40% of free cash flow is returned via the $0.45 quarterly dividend and the NCIB. Implies a modest discount to the ~$215-$227 analyst consensus target range.

risks: Gold breaks toward $3,400-$3,800/oz as 30-year Treasury yields hold above 5.5% and the Fed tightens again
Barnat remediation slips, pushing the Canadian Malartic production shortfall past 150koz in 2027 and 2028
AISC breaches the $1,550/oz upper guidance bound on diesel (Nunavut sealift purchased ~30% above budget), labour and royalty inflation
Cash taxes of $3.4-$3.6B plus capex above $3.0B compress free cash flow if realized prices fall faster than costs
Further safety incidents following the April and May 2026 fatalities force extended stoppages

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results (after market close; call October 29) — first full quarter reflecting the Barnat suspension
Federal Reserve October policy decision — markets priced a ~73% hike probability in late September, the dominant swing factor for gold
Barnat open pit mining expected to resume at Canadian Malartic after remediation
Completion of the internal technical evaluation for Odyssey Shaft #2
FY2026 results, 2027 guidance, updated three-year outlook and year-end reserve statement
First shaft-hoisted production from East Gouldie via Odyssey Shaft #1
Gold price direction, real yields and central bank demand

key_risks: Gold price leverage cuts both ways — gold has fallen from a $4,696/oz peak on August 25, 2026 to roughly $4,150-$4,300/oz by late September
Barnat rock mass movement reduces production by 60-80koz in H2 2026 and up to 150koz in each of 2027 and 2028, and lifts Canadian Malartic total cash costs to ~$1,260/oz for 2026
Cost inflation: diesel for the Nunavut sealift was bought ~30% above budget; royalties scale with the gold price
Capex raised to $2.6-$2.8B excluding capitalized exploration (from $2.2-$2.4B) on the Hope Bay construction decision
Safety and social licence risk after fatal accidents at Canadian Malartic (April 2026) and Upper Beaver (May 2026)
FX exposure to CAD, EUR, AUD and MXN against a stronger US dollar
Dilution and contingent liability from the Rupert acquisition, including 207.7 million outstanding CVRs worth up to C$3.00 each
